assumptions: Memory-augmented architectures retain internal state representing historical trajectory.
Agents employ a discount factor weighting recent and historical rewards.
Deterministic gridworld environments isolate path-dependence from stochastic noise.
definition.falsification: Measured divergence slope is positive or zero, indicating stable or increasing preference divergence over time.
definition.statement: Memory-augmented agents exhibit transient state-dependent variance that decays over time, rather than stable path-dependent preference formation, measurable as policy divergence that decreases with increased training duration in deterministic gridworld environments.
definition.uncertainty: It remains unclear if any long-term stability exists or if all path-dependent signals are purely transient.

definition.method: Run training on 20x20 gridworld; measure policy divergence at multiple intervals (10k, 50k, 100k, 200k steps) to calculate the divergence decay slope.
definition.success: Slope of divergence is statistically less than 0, indicating decay.

proposal.summary: Revising the path-dependence hypothesis to test for transient variance versus stable preference formation and initiating an experiment to measure divergence decay.
proposal.title: Revision of Preference Formation Hypothesis
